headline.text: The FDA label says alcohol combined with perampanel significantly worsened mood and increased anger.

reported.text: The label reports worsened mood and increased anger with the combination.
It also describes a possible increase in CNS depression with concomitant alcohol.
The EMA perampanel label reports additive or supra-additive effects with alcohol on alertness and vigilance tasks in healthy subjects.

claims.text: The FDA label says alcohol combined with perampanel significantly worsened mood and increased anger.
claims.quote: The combination of alcohol and perampanel significantly worsened mood and increased anger.
claims.judgeRationale: The label states verbatim that the combination of alcohol and perampanel significantly worsened mood and increased anger.

claims.text: The FDA label says concomitant alcohol and perampanel may increase CNS depression.
claims.quote: The concomitant use of perampanel and CNS depressants including alcohol may increase CNS depression.
claims.judgeRationale: The label says concomitant perampanel and CNS depressants including alcohol may increase CNS depression.

claims.text: The EMA perampanel label reports additive or supra-additive effects with alcohol on alertness and vigilance tasks in healthy subjects.
claims.quote: The effects of perampanel on tasks involving alertness and vigilance such as driving ability were additive or supra-additive to the effects of alcohol itself, as found in a pharmacodynamic interaction study in healthy subjects.
claims.judgeRationale: Independent Claude Opus 5.5 review against the full EMA SmPC section 4.5, supplied in the implementation brief: supports the claim.

sources.title: Fycompa: 4.5
sources.citation: European Medicines Agency, Fycompa, https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/product-information/fycompa-epar-product-information_en.pdf, accessed 2026-11. Extracted SmPC sections, whitespace normalised; no endorsement. SmPC 4.5

pharmacistQuestions.text: The label describes this interaction, but there seem to be no human studies of it. How is it usually handled for someone like me?
Do any of my other medicines or products, like cough syrup or mouthwash, contain alcohol?
Does my dose, or the time between taking Perampanel and drinking alcohol, change how much this matters?
